ops.title: fusekit's session roles collapse onto lane alone — Schema is a build era, not a peer identity
ops.body:
Established 2026-08-01. This corrects two assumptions the orchestrator had been carrying.

**Correction 1: the roles do not become `Schema` membership.** `Schema` is the renamed `wire_build`
digest — "one application-protocol era a build speaks or still accepts" (daemon.go:62-63), a flat
compat ladder tested by linear membership (`internal/wire/hello.go:53-61`), which only ever admits
or refuses and only on the business lane (`internal/wire/server.go:249-252`). A control hello must
not carry one at all. Stuffing role names into `Schemas` would consume the whole list and leave no
room for a genuine prior era.

**Correction 2: it is a rename, not a new concept.** fusekit's pinned 0.20.9 hello carried
`{protocol, wire_build, role}`; main carries `{protocol, lane, schema, nonce}`. `wire_build` →
`schema` (the rejection name survives as `ResponseCodeBuildMismatch`), `role` → `lane`. fusekit
already passes the digest at both call sites; it just gets renamed.

**Verdict: SessionLane needs no third case.** fusekit's three Swift roles (and its Go mirror's seven)
collapse onto `lane` alone: broker's fd handoff → control (daemonkit now hardcodes this — 
`BrokerHandoffClient` dials `lane: .control` internally and `brokerHandoffOp` refuses any other);
`broker.open` → business; brokerLifecycle → business (its receipt/readiness authority is gone as a
concept — the phase stream now publishes to every session); fileProviderExtension → business. All
four role files delete, Swift and Go.

What did NOT have a home was on a third axis entirely — see
[[trust-business-widens-to-a-requirement-set]].

**Swift break list at main** — exactly four fusekit files import DaemonKit, no `@_exported import`,
so this is the whole surface. Broken: `SocketClient.init` (`wireBuild:`/`role:` → `schema:`/`lane:`),
`RuntimeClientConfiguration.init` (same, plus `noProgressTimeout:` deleted outright and `onProgress:`
added), `BrokerSocketBridge.init` (5 args → 3; `handoffRole:` and `expectedRuntimeBuild:` both gone).
Everything else fusekit touches survives unchanged: `AppGroupContainer` and its nested types,
`SocketClient.Configuration` (all 7 fields), `open`/`call`/`close`/`events`, `SocketCall`,
`SocketChunkStream`, `SocketEventStream`, `SocketTerminal`.

**A constraint worth knowing before designing anything onto the control lane:** it admits exactly ONE
session server-wide (`internal/wire/server.go:105` `controlSlot`, asserted at
roundtrip_test.go:288-291), and a broker's handoff generation holds it for up to 256 handoffs.
